projects.title: Automated eDNA MinION Pipeline
projects.description: Project-local, reproducible pipeline for processing MinION amplicon reads, mapping to a Sanger reference DB and producing species-by-sample matrices plus consensus-based validation.
projects.body:
Context: As part of the GenoRobotics initiative, this project focuses on biodiversity monitoring in the Udzungwa Mountains (Tanzania). The goal was to develop a fully automated, scalable bioinformatics pipeline capable of processing on-site Oxford Nanopore (MinION) sequencing data. The pipeline identifies amphibian and mammal species (e.g., Leptopelis, Rhynchocyon) by comparing environmental DNA (eDNA) reads against a Sanger reference database.

My Contributions

I designed and implemented the end-to-end Python pipeline, transitioning the workflow from manual analysis to a reproducible automated system. My key technical contributions included:

  • Pipeline Architecture: Built a modular, linear workflow integrating standard tools (cutadapt, minimap2, samtools) to process raw FASTQ data through to species matrices.
  • Consensus-Based Validation (Step 5): I introduced a critical validation step that separates "High Abundance" (quantitative) from "True Identity" (qualitative). By generating consensus sequences for high-count targets and re-aligning them to the database, the system prevents false positives caused by PCR bias or sequencing noise.
  • Reproducibility: Packaged all dependencies in a local Conda environment to ensure the pipeline is portable and can run on standard field laptops.

Results & Analysis

The automated pipeline achieved 100% concordance in species identification compared to the manual methods used in the original Menegon et al. study. The matrix generation successfully filtered noise (requiring MAPQ > 40) to produce clear abundance signals.

The consensus validation step proved essential for interpreting results. For example, while Leptopelis CO1 showed very high abundance (27k reads), the validation revealed a low identity match (17.2%), flagging it for manual inspection rather than blind acceptance. Conversely, species like Sorex alpinus were validated with high confidence.

projects.title: LMMs-Eval: Evaluation Suite of Large Multimodal Models
projects.description: Extended the open-source LMMs-Eval framework to wildlife video datasets (MammAlps, AnimalKingdom), benchmarking InternVL3-8B on species and behaviour recognition with reproducible pipelines and standardised metrics.
projects.presentation: /assets/Benchmarking VLMs for Animal Behavior Analysis with LMMs-Eval.pdf
projects.body:
Context: This project was my Summer 2025 (Jul–Sep) research internship with the Mathis Group. The goal was to address a key gap in AI: most VLM benchmarks are human-centric and fail to test models on complex ecological tasks. I extended the existing open-source LMMs-Eval framework to create a standardized, reproducible benchmark for animal behavior analysis using real-world wildlife datasets.

What I implemented

  • Extended the lmms-eval framework to support new wildlife video datasets (MammAlps and AnimalKingdom).
  • Authored a "universal dataset builder" script to standardize annotations from JSONL files, process videos, and generate HuggingFace-ready datasets.
  • Defined and implemented new evaluation tasks for species, action, and activity recognition.
  • Implemented and registered a Jaccard Index metric to evaluate multi-label predictions and check for partial correctness.
  • Integrated the InternVL3-8B model into the framework for benchmarking.
  • Engineered a robust parsing logic to reliably extract <answer> tags from model outputs, achieving 100% success on compliant answers and eliminating malformed results seen in baseline tests.
  • Standardized the folder structure for results to automate report generation and simplify debugging.

My contributions

My primary contribution was building the end-to-end reproducible pipeline on top of the existing framework. I was responsible for all dataset processing, task implementation, and metric registration within the lmms-eval framework. I conducted a rigorous comparative analysis between my new pipeline and the original workshop (baseline) results. My analysis confirmed the reproducibility of action recognition, identified key discrepancies in other tasks (likely due to video preprocessing differences), and demonstrated that my pipeline produced cleaner, more reliable parsing than the baseline.

projects.title: EPFL AI Tutor (NLP Course Project)
projects.description: As part of a 4-person team, we built a specialized AI tutor for EPFL course content. We fine-tuned a 0.6B LLM using DPO, RAG, and Quantization. My specific role was implementing the quantized pipeline.
projects.body:
Context: For the CS-552 (Modern NLP) course project, our team (Al et fines herbes) fine-tuned the Qwen3-0.6B-Base model to create a specialized AI tutor for advanced STEM Multiple Choice Question Answering (MCQA). We implemented several variants: a model aligned using Stepwise Direct Preference Optimization (SDPO), a Supervised Fine-Tuned (SFT) MCQA model, a memory-efficient Quantized model, and a knowledge-enhanced Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) model.

My Contributions

As part of the 4-person team, I was primarily responsible for developing and evaluating the Quantized model variant.

Lead: Quantized Model

  • Implemented a post-training quantization (PTQ) pipeline using the llmcompressor library to reduce the model size.
  • Focused on a single-pass, oneshot PTQ approach, applying symmetric per-channel weight quantization and per-tensor activation clipping.
  • Experimented with various quantization schemes (W8A8, W4A16, W4A4) and calibration dataset sizes (e.g., 1024, 2048 samples) to find the optimal trade-off between accuracy and memory efficiency.
  • Benchmarked the different quantized configurations for MCQA accuracy and peak VRAM usage on a subset of STEMQA prompts.
  • Identified the W8A8-1024 configuration as the best performer, achieving slightly higher accuracy than the full-precision model with the best accuracy-to-VRAM ratio.
  • Configured the model's quantization_config file and uploaded the final W8A8-1024 quantized model checkpoints to HuggingFace for evaluation.

Shared Responsibilities

In addition to my lead role on the quantized model, I collaborated with the team on several tasks:

  • Collected and manually labeled preference data derived from ChatGPT interactions using the provided GPT Wrapper for the DPO training phase.
  • Contributed to preprocessing datasets like UltraFeedback and StackExchange to filter for STEM content and establish difficulty rankings for SDPO training.
  • Participated in writing the literature review, progress report, and the final 6-page project report.
  • Ensured reproducibility by documenting methods and contributing to the shared training codebase.

Results & Analysis

Our final combined model (DPO + SFT3) showed improvements over the base Qwen3-0.6B model on several benchmarks, although the gains were often within the standard deviation range. The SDPO approach generally outperformed standard DPO, demonstrating the benefit of curriculum learning for preference alignment.

My work on quantization demonstrated that the W8A8-1024 scheme provided the best balance: it maintained (and slightly improved) accuracy compared to the full-precision MCQA model while reducing memory footprint, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained hardware. More aggressive quantization like W4A4 significantly degraded performance.

Table comparing key quantization results.

Ethical Considerations

We discussed the ethical implications, including the English-language bias of the base model and the need for careful adaptation for other languages, especially low-resource ones. We also noted how quantization could improve accessibility by enabling deployment on less powerful devices, but carries risks of exacerbating performance disparities across different knowledge domains or dialects if not carefully validated.

projects.title: Movie Violence and Crime Correlation Analysis
projects.description: Owned the real-world crime data pipeline for a team project. I explored, extracted, and cleaned daily US crime statistics (NIBRS) to engineer the weekly 'violence score,' the key dependent variable for our team's ARDL time-series model.
projects.body:
Context: This project investigated whether the prevalence of violent movies correlates with real-world violence in the US. We analyzed 17,000+ movies (from CMU and Kaggle datasets) against US crime statistics (from the NIBRS dataset). To isolate the impact, we implemented an auto-regressive distributed lag (ARDL) model with time-fixed effects. Our study found no statistically significant correlation based on the available data.

What I implemented

  • Managed the complete data pipeline for all real-world violence data, using the NIBRS dataset.
  • Performed extensive data exploration, extraction, and cleaning to prepare the raw, daily-level crime statistics for time-series analysis.
  • Engineered the primary "violence score," a weekly aggregated metric that served as the key dependent variable for the team's ARDL model.
  • Created plots and visualizations to analyze and present the trends and patterns in the real-world violence data over time.

My contributions

In this team project, my primary responsibility was owning the "real-world violence" half of the equation. I sourced, processed, and modeled all crime data from the NIBRS database, transforming raw daily reports into a clean, robust weekly time-series. The "violence score" I engineered was the core variable our team used to test our hypothesis. I also produced the visualizations for this data, which helped inform the ARDL model's design and interpret the final results.

projects.title: Machine Learning for Plasma Transition Detection
projects.description: Developed time-series models (Bi-LSTM, Uni-LSTM) to detect H-L back-transitions in tokamak plasma. I implemented the full data preprocessing pipeline, engineered feature sets (including FFT), and systematically evaluated model performance (F1 Score: 0.72).
projects.body:
Context: In a tokamak, plasma can exist in a Low (L) confinement mode or a more stable, High (H) confinement mode. This project focuses on detecting the "back-transition" from H mode to L mode, a critical event to understand for maintaining plasma stability. The objective was to use machine learning to identify these transitions from complex time-series data and analyze the conditions that lead to them.

What I implemented

  • Data Exploration & Selection: Analyzed and segmented raw experimental data, separating 35 unusable experiments (due to missing features like DML) to create a clean 'selected experiments' dataset for training.
  • Signal Preprocessing Pipeline: Developed the Python preprocessing pipeline to handle the complex time-series data. This included linear interpolation for missing values, applying Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) to the Halpha13 signal as an optional feature, and normalizing features.
  • Model Development: Implemented, trained, and evaluated time-series models to classify transitions, primarily a Bidirectional-LSTM (Bi-LSTM) and a Unidirectional-LSTM (Uni-LSTM), using PyTorch and TensorFlow.
  • Feature Engineering: Defined and tested multiple feature sets (e.g., features1, features2) combining parameters like plasma energy (Wtot), magnetic signals (DML), and density/temperature profiles.
  • Hyperparameter Optimization: Used Optuna to automate hyperparameter tuning to improve model performance.

My contributions

My role in this project was to help build the end-to-end machine learning pipeline. I was heavily involved in exploring the raw tokamak shot data, writing the Python scripts to clean and preprocess the signals, and engineering the feature sets for the models. I implemented both the Uni-LSTM and Bi-LSTM architectures, customized their time-window parameters, and ran a systematic evaluation to determine the best-performing model and feature combination.

Results

We systematically evaluated both models against different feature sets and preprocessing options. The Bi-LSTM model clearly outperformed the Uni-LSTM, achieving a top F1 Score of 0.7163 on the test set, as shown in the summary of best results below.

projects.title: Cadmium Catcher: Live Biotherapeutic Product (iGEM)
projects.description: Contributed to the project from conception to production, including wet lab work. I also led the web development, designing and coding the official website to communicate our science, which helped win the 'Best Education Prize'.
projects.body:
Context: Cadmium is a toxic heavy metal and carcinogen that contaminates soil and water, bioaccumulating in crops and posing a serious risk for chronic human exposure. Our iGEM team engineered a live biotherapeutic product (LBP): a modified E. coli designed to "catch" cadmium ions in the intestine. The engineered bacteria express a mucus-binding protein (SpaC) to anchor in the gut and a cadmium-specific binding protein (EC20) to sequester the metal, which is then safely cleared from the body.

My Contributions

As a multidisciplinary team member, I contributed to both the wet lab engineering and the final digital presentation of the project.

Wet Lab & Project Development

  • Participated in the initial project conception and design of our synthetic biology solution.
  • Performed hands-on wet lab work, including molecular cloning, bacterial transformations, and protein expression assays.
  • Contributed to the team's research and development efforts in producing the final live biotherapeutic product.

Web Development & Science Communication

  • Led the development of the entire official project website from scratch using React.JS, HTML, and CSS.
  • Translated complex synthetic biology concepts into accessible web content, including graphics, diagrams, and written explanations.
  • Produced educational materials for outreach, which was a key component of our "Best Education Prize" win.

Awards & Recognition

  • Gold Medal
  • Best Education Prize Winner
  • Best Therapeutics Project Nominee
  • Safety and Security Award Nominee
